concept.title: Through-going field depends on surface orientation
concept.inferential_jump: Magnetic flux measures the component of magnetic field through an oriented area; changing the surface orientation changes flux even when B and area size stay fixed.
entry_assumptions: R1: magnetic field B is an axial directed quantity with explicit in-plane and out-of-plane representation conventions.

teaching_path.action: Attach a normal arrow to the surface before comparing orientations, so the face has an explicit through-direction.
teaching_path.why_valid: A flat surface alone has no preferred side; the normal supplies the orientation needed to distinguish with-through from against-through.

teaching_path.action: Rotate the same loop from face-on to tilted to edge-on while leaving its size and the surrounding field unchanged.
teaching_path.why_valid: Only orientation changes, so any change in through-going field is attributable to how the surface faces the field rather than to a stronger field or larger loop.
teaching_path.output: face-on -> most through; tilted -> less through; edge-on -> none through

teaching_path.action: Keep the physical surface fixed but reverse which normal arrow is declared positive.
teaching_path.why_valid: Changing the chosen orientation reverses the sign convention while leaving the physical setup unchanged, separating signed description from apparatus.
teaching_path.output: normal one way -> one sign; reversed normal -> opposite sign

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Flux is just magnetic-field strength times area, so orientation does not matter.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: A loop with fixed area rotates from face-on to edge-on in a uniform field. What must happen to its flux?
misconceptions.repair: Project the oriented area along the field direction: the dot product selects the component through the surface.

exit_task.prompt: Three identical loops sit in the same uniform magnetic field: one face-on, one tilted, and one edge-on. Rank the amount of field passing through them and explain the role of the chosen surface normal.

answer.summary: The face-on loop has the greatest through-going field, the tilted loop has less, and the edge-on loop has none; the normal states which side counts as the positive orientation.
reasoning: The field strength and loop area are held fixed, so orientation is the only changing feature.
A face presented to the field admits the greatest through-going component, while an edge presented to it admits none.
Reversing the named normal changes the sign convention but not the physical loop or field.
answer.check: Imagine rotating only the loop continuously from face-on to edge-on; the ranking should change smoothly without any appeal to a stronger or weaker field.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: The exit answer ranks orientations and explains sign choice qualitatively; it contains no computed numerical result.
